body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{T\subseteq\mathcal V:|T|=r,\ \exists t\text{ ordering }T\text{ with }Q_{tt}\succ0\text{ and }L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}\text{ diagonal and nonnegative for every }e\}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent multi-sample Gaussian covariance experiment across environments \(e\in\mathcal E\).
sampling_model.units: For each environment, \(n_e\) independent centered observations \(Y_{ei}\in\mathbb R^d\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown soft interventions change exactly \(r\) observed structural-noise variances; the fixed baseline is a minimum-variance condition and a designed reference environment increases every target variance.
sampling_model.overlap: Covariances obey \(mI_d\preceq\Sigma_e\preceq MI_d\); no separation from profile collisions is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical covariance tuple is used directly; stationary latent confounding and measurement error cancel in population covariance differences.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 characterizes the LIT output under latent confounding as a candidate superset of the observed intervention targets.
Theorem 1 gives uniqueness of the global joint diagonalizer if and only if every pair of intervention-variance profiles is noncollinear.
The identifiability theorem recovers the unmixing matrix up to scaling and permutation when differenced diagonal profiles are pairwise noncollinear.

In arXiv v1, Theorems 1--3 establish sign-and-permutation equivalence, point identification under distinct variance-ratio eigenvalues, and the eigen-decomposition representation; Section III, Definition 4, and the later point- and set-identification subsections characterize restricted rotation sets under eigenvalue multiplicity.
Theorem 1 constructs a test-inversion confidence set for a causal effect while retaining uncertainty over two linear causal structures.
The paper constructs random sets with pointwise and uniform asymptotic coverage for an identified set and its images by objective-function inversion.
Theorems 1--2 give weak-identification-robust chi-square inference for full and selected structural parameters in heteroskedastic models.

body.tldr: Under a designed minimum-variance baseline and a common reference environment that increases every target variance, stationary latent confounding and measurement error disappear from covariance differences, but collisions among structural-variance profiles destroy unique global diagonalization.  The complete labeled target fiber is identified instead: a size-\(r\) set is compatible exactly when some ordering passes a positive principal-block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) certificate, and every certificate has a legal acyclic Gaussian realization at any positive-definite baseline with strictly positive structural and measurement noises.  Explicit boundary witnesses show that signed shifts invalidate the nonnegative-diagonal test and that removing the common reference destroys the rank-\(r\) carrier.  A subset-memoized pivot recursion computes all compatible sets, while measurable feasible-point augmentation yields always-nonempty honest family regions; classification information distance gives matching consistency and impossibility regimes near profile collisions.

project_justification.gap: Unknown-target methods with latent confounding return candidate supersets, whereas covariance-difference methods recover a global mixing matrix only under profile separation.  Bacchiocchi et al. first give sign/permutation, distinct-eigenvalue, and eigen-decomposition results and later study multiplicity through restricted HSVAR rotation sets, not the complete family of observed causal target labels.
project_justification.niche: With a designed minimum-variance baseline and a common reference that changes all targets, acyclicity supplies a triangular labeling constraint that survives profile collisions and can be checked on candidate target principal blocks even when individual changed columns are not identified.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an if-and-only-if labeled-fiber theorem, an arbitrary-baseline positive-noise converse, a precise boundary result for signed shifts and split references, a complete subset recursion, and honest classification inference whose nonclosed-model selector and information boundary remain valid at covariance-profile collisions.

body.related_work: Yang, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash motivate the target-matching problem and show that their latent-confounded LIT output is a superset rather than the exact target set.  BACKSHIFT and coroICA provide the covariance-differencing and joint-diagonalization ancestors; their broader shift formulations motivate the method, while the nonnegative fixed-baseline and common-reference restrictions here are new panel-design conditions rather than inherited BACKSHIFT assumptions.  Yang et al. analyze measurement error after assuming a recoverable mixing matrix; here invariant positive measurement error cancels before the target fiber is characterized.  In Bacchiocchi et al., arXiv v1 Theorems 1--3 establish sign/permutation equivalence, distinct-eigenvalue point identification, and the eigen-decomposition representation.  Their multiplicity object appears later in Section III, Definition 4 and the point- and set-identification subsections: an admissible rotation set for structural parameters and impulse responses under zero and sign restrictions.  The present fiber intersects covariance-shift factorizations with unit-lower acyclicity and observed labels, producing a strictly different and more constrained discrete object rather than extending those three preliminary theorems.  Jaber et al. and Squires et al. make completeness over unknown-target equivalence classes algorithmically central under graphical oracle conditions; the present recursion uses exact covariance pivots.  Brown--Purves measurable selection and Romano--Shaikh identified-set inversion motivate the inference construction, while Lewis motivates treating near-proportional profiles as weak identification.  Wu et al. provide the concrete consumer: perturbation-target prediction under acknowledged unseen-confounder limitations, for which the proposed output is an honest effective-target family only when the narrower covariance model is defensible.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The model assumes environment-invariant structural coefficients, latent covariance, and measurement-error covariance, a fixed dimension, exact rank \(r\), common shift range, a designed minimum-variance baseline, and one reference environment with a positive increment at every target.  The boundary proposition shows that signed shifts invalidate the nonnegative certificate and that a panel without a common reference requires an aggregate multi-environment carrier instead of \(Q\).  If latent factors or measurement errors change with the environment, covariance differencing need not isolate observed structural-noise shifts.  The semialgebraic algorithm is a certification route, not a claim of transcriptome-scale computation, and the biological labels are effective structural-noise targets rather than direct binding sites.
body.honest_scope: The exact fiber, positive-noise realization, design-restriction boundary, subset recursion, measurable approximate selector, finite-sample family coverage, and two-regime information boundary are theorem targets.  The finite-sample sufficient threshold is \(\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)>2c_{\alpha}+1\) on the stated confidence event, with the full \(x\)-indexed bound retained for consistency.  The exact local minimax power envelope at bounded information distance is deliberately open.  When \(r=1\), the proposal reduces to the familiar rank-one ambiguity \(\{\{j\}:Q_{jj}>0\}\); no stronger single-target identification is claimed.
